data.name: Vietnam
data.summary: Vietnam taxes residents on worldwide income, but investment income bears low flat rates: 5% on dividends, 0.1% of proceeds on securities sales, 2% of proceeds on real estate and 20% on gains from private company stakes. Inheritances and gifts above VND 20 million are taxed at 10% personal income tax, with exemptions for real estate within the close family. There is no wealth tax. Long-term residence for a non-working foreign family is difficult: there is no investor-residence programme beyond investor visas tied to a Vietnamese business.

regimes.name: Vietnamese tax resident
regimes.description: Worldwide income; flat schedular rates on investment income: 5% dividends, 0.1% of securities proceeds, 2% of real estate proceeds; 10% on inheritances.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if present 183 days or more in a calendar year or in 12 consecutive months from arrival, or having a permanent residence (including a rented home with a definite lease term).

capital_gains.summary: Tax residents are taxed on worldwide income. Non-employment income is taxed at flat rates on gross amounts: sale of securities 0.1% of the sale proceeds, transfer of capital contributions 20% of the net gain (or 2% of proceeds), sale of real estate 2% of the sale proceeds. PwC does not distinguish Vietnamese from foreign securities, so the 0.1%-of-proceeds rule is applied to foreign listed shares too.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: The PwC tables (five-band employment schedule, VND 20 million thresholds, alternative 2%-of-proceeds basis for capital assignments) appear to reflect the new Personal Income Tax Law adopted in 2025; its number and effective date were not verified. How foreign securities are taxed in practice (0.1% of proceeds vs capital-assignment rules) is uncertain.

open_questions: Application of the 0.1%-of-proceeds rule to foreign-listed securities not confirmed.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Proceeds-based rates converted to a rate on the gain assuming the gain is half of the proceeds: securities 0.1% of proceeds -> 0.2%; real estate 2% of proceeds -> 4%. Private company (capital assignment): 20% of net gain. Headline 20% = capital assignment rate.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Business income of individuals is taxed at 0.5%-5% of revenue or 15%-20% of profit (PwC); not normally relevant to a private investor.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide taxation for residents with credit for foreign PIT, capped at the Vietnamese tax on that income.

dividends.summary: Dividends (and non-bank interest) received by residents are taxed at a flat 5%. Foreign dividends of residents are included under the worldwide principle at the same 5%, with a credit for foreign tax capped at the Vietnamese tax, so treaty withholding of 10%-15% normally absorbs it.

dividends.rate_basis: Flat 5% on gross dividends (PwC). Foreign: 5% before credit; with 10%+ source WHT the net Vietnamese tax is nil.
dividends.withholding_outbound: No WHT on dividends paid by Vietnamese companies to foreign corporate shareholders; individuals pay 5% (corporate summary, not opened).
dividends.treaty_network: DTAs with 81 jurisdictions, of which several (including the United States) are not yet in force (PwC).

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Non-agricultural land use tax at low rates (0.03%-0.15%; not verified). Registration fee 0.5% on property transfers. A tax on second homes has been discussed (not in force as far as checked).

inheritance.summary: Vietnam has no separate inheritance or gift tax, but personal income tax of 10% applies to inheritances and gifts (securities, capital contributions, real estate and other registered assets) above VND 20 million. Inheritances and gifts of real estate between parents and children, spouses, grandparents and grandchildren, and siblings are exempt; other assets such as securities passed to children are taxed at 10% (exemption list from general knowledge of the PIT Law, not verified).

open_questions: Scope for foreign assets and the parent-child exemption for non-real-estate assets were not verified in the law.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts above VND 20 million taxed at 10% on the recipient on the same basis as inheritances; real estate between parents and children exempt.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Unclear whether foreign securities inherited by a resident heir are caught; the tax applies to assets whose ownership must be registered (Vietnamese securities, capital contributions, real estate, vehicles), so foreign portfolio holdings may fall outside it in practice (not verified).
inheritance.domicile_rules: Recipient-based: a resident heir is taxed on taxable inheritances; non-residents on Vietnamese assets.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if present 183 days or more in the calendar year or in the 12 consecutive months from arrival, or having a permanent residence in Vietnam (registered residence or a rented house with a definite lease term).

routes.requirements: Temporary residence tied to capital invested in a Vietnamese enterprise (tiers by amount; not verified). No passive residence-by-investment programme was found.

income.name: Vietnam

income_tax.summary: Residents pay 5% to 35% on employment income under a five-bracket schedule, after a VND 15.5 million monthly (VND 186 million a year) personal deduction for tax periods from 1 January 2026 (Resolution 110/2025). The new Personal Income Tax Law 109/2025/QH15 takes effect 1 July 2026; KPMG and Rödl report its resident salary and wage rules, and the five brackets, as applying from the 2026 tax period. Residents are taxed on worldwide income. Self-employed business income is taxed on revenue (0.5-5%) or profit (15-20%), with a revenue threshold below which no PIT is due (PwC: VND 1 billion; KPMG and Rödl report VND 500 million under the new law). Employees pay 9% social and health insurance up to VND 50.6 million a month.
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Employee: social insurance 8% + health insurance 1% (as listed by PwC) on salary up to 20x the statutory base salary (VND 50.6 million a month from 1 July 2026, VND 46.8 million before); unemployment insurance 1% is for Vietnamese only. The annual cap shown uses VND 50.6 million x 12. SI needs a work permit and a Vietnamese labour contract of one year or more; HI applies from one month. Independent foreign contractors have no mandatory SI. Business income: 0.5-5% of revenue or 15-20% of profit; PIT-free revenue threshold: PwC says VND 1 billion; KPMG (24 Feb 2026) and Rödl (Feb 2026) report a rise from VND 100 million to VND 500 million under Law 109/2025, so treat VND 1 billion as unconfirmed.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No local income tax. Dependant deduction VND 6.2 million a month each (Resolution 110/2025).

income.residence_routes: EU, US and other citizens: Vietnam has no digital nomad visa as of February 2026; remote workers rely on visa exemption (about 14-45 days by nationality) or the 90-day multiple-entry e-visa, which is a tourist permit so working remotely sits in a grey area. Skilled employees need a work permit and temporary residence card via a Vietnamese employer; a five-year Talent Visa launched in August 2025 for high-profile professionals. Work permit rules were not researched in detail.
open_questions: No nomad visa; no expat tax regime found.
Work permit and residence card requirements not researched.
2-bedroom rent is a USD guide range midpoint without a stated method.

succession.name: Vietnam
succession.summary: Minor children, adult children who cannot work, a spouse and parents are guaranteed two thirds of their intestate share whatever the will says (Civil Code art. 644). A foreigner's estate follows the law of their nationality, but Vietnamese property rules still apply to land and housing. Vietnam has no trust law and the Hague Trusts Convention is not in force.
succession.reserved_share: Minor children, adult children unable to work, spouse and parents: at least two thirds of the share they would take on intestacy (Civil Code 2015 art. 644).
succession.foreign_law_note: A law-firm source reports art. 680: inheritance follows the law of the country of which the deceased was a citizen at death, with Vietnamese law for immovables in Vietnam and for formalities. I did not read the article. A foreigner's ownership of land and housing in Vietnam is restricted by other laws.
succession.trust_note: Not on the HCCH status table. Vietnam has no trust law; the Civil Code has agency and property management contracts only. Foreign trusts are not recognised in practice. Social and charity funds are under Decree 93/2019/ND-CP, for non-profit purposes only.
open_questions: Read Civil Code art. 680-681 and the 2015 Code's text of art. 644 from an official source.
Confirm Decree 93/2019 is still the current fund regime and whether the 2023 Land Law limits foreign heirs.
